text:
Lina: seeing a big uptick in 429s from /v1/embeddings/rerank in us-west1 since ~10:30. tail latency spikes and immediate rejections when qps > ~90. anyone touching admission control or lanes? :warning:
infra-bot: ALERT: embeddings.rerank.queue_rejections (us-west1) increased by 350% over 5m. top hosts: gpu-wst-12..15 at 96-99% util.
Jasper: we moved a couple internal search jobs to embeddings yesterday — could be causing KV cache churn and bumping concurrent usage. rerank is heavier on sequence length and tends to blow through per-worker concurrency.
Kai: confirmed cluster heatmap — us-west1 dedicated pool is saturated. autoscaler didn't add nodes because reserved capacity floor hit. network egress to us-east1 is fine but will add ~40ms median and some cost.
Monica: CS flagged two customers experiencing timeouts during large rerank batches (30-50 queries). they're on Dedicated but no lane pinning.
Arjun: we can do a quick admission tweak: split rerank traffic into its own lane with stricter concurrency and a small queue to avoid cross-impact. pushing config is fast.
Jasper: proposed lane config (rough sketch):
```yaml
admission_control:
  lanes:
    - name: embeddings-default
      qps_limit: 150
      concurrency_limit: 64
      queue_limit: 200
    - name: embeddings-rerank
      qps_limit: 40
      concurrency_limit: 8
      queue_limit: 40
  fallback: rate_limit
```
Jasper: idea is rerank gets isolated concurrency so one heavy workload doesn't evict other embeddings work. also prefer request-slot admission rather than token-count for rerank since it spikes seq length unpredictably.
Arjun: I can apply a temporary policy. doing dry-run then swap. curl to apply:
```bash
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/admission/policy \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d @rerank-lanes.yaml
```
Kai: quick note — if we redirect rerank to a new lane that targets a different GPU pool, ensure node labels and quantization profiles match (we have a few older cards in us-east that don't support int4 paths). fallback will need model-variant mapping.
Jasper: good catch. will set lane -> model_variant mapping to prefer fp16-quantized variant when moving across regions.
Monica: timeline: can we isolate within 15-20m and notify CS? customers want mitigation asap.
Arjun: applying lane config now as a canary to 10% of traffic for rerank in us-west1. will scale to 100% if rejection rate drops.
deploy-bot: rollout started: admission-policy-update @arjun (canary: 10%).
Lina: thx, watching metrics.
infra-bot: patch applied to control plane. monitoring hooks enabled.
Jasper: if rejections persist we should also consider: 1) per-customer backpressure (soft limits), 2) automatic burst window with short token-prices, 3) prefilling KV cache for common prefixes.
Kai: 10m in: gpu-wst-12 still hot but queue_rejections down 70% for canary slice. overall p50/p95 latencies slightly up (10-20ms) — expected.
Monica: CS note: told customers we isolated rerank traffic and expect normal behavior soon. they appreciate transparency.
Arjun: canary -> 100% now. deploy-bot: rollout complete.
deploy-bot: rollout complete: admission-policy-update @arjun (100%).
Lina: rejections are back down to baseline. nice.
Kai: follow-up question: do we want to spin ephemeral GPUs in us-west1 for peak windows? cost tradeoff vs cross-region egress and latency. I can run numbers.
Jasper: yes, let's run a quick cost vs SLA calc. for short bursts ephemeral nodes might beat customer impact. also long-term: more aggressive autoscale policies per-lane.
Monica: please cc me on the cost calc; CS needs thresholds to communicate.
Arjun: I'll open a short runbook for lane emergency ops (how to split lanes, revert, and cost thresholds).
Lina: closing loop — thanks all. will follow up if we see second wave.
